sentences.text: The thesis's central claim is unsupported. The record confirms that Huang resigned on November 11, 2026, but nothing in it links his departure to later earnings, cash flow or valuation, so 'because Jensen is gone' is a reason the record cannot test.

Every financial figure here predates the resignation. The newest quarter ends 2026-07-26 and the valuation uses a 2026-09-30 price, so the record cannot show how the business or the market responded to the change.

The pre-departure business the thesis leans on is mixed. Gross margin held above 70% for four quarters and revenue doubled in the newest quarter, yet the fiscal 2026 doubling claim fails and free cash flow ran below net income.

At the 2026-09-30 price the reverse DCF needs 13.4% a year for 10 years. The assumption it leans on most is a 65.2% operating margin held every year, which is exactly what a leadership transition puts in question, not something the departure supports.

The 28.5× multiple is paid on net income that converted to operating cash at only 0.70x over the trailing four quarters and 0.40x in the newest quarter, so the earnings the price rests on are weaker in cash than they look.

A careful investor would next want an 8-K naming a permanent chief executive and the first 10-Q covering a quarter after November 2026, read for operating margin, receivables and inventory against the levels the price assumes.
All three corollaries of c1 hold, but each compares quarters that ended before the resignation. They describe the business Huang ran, and none of it can be credited to his absence.

The resignation follows other 2026 senior exits: the chief accounting officer and the head of worldwide field operations both announced retirements, and the CFO now serves as interim CEO. The record therefore shows turnover, not an identifiable improvement.

The thesis's best financial evidence is the margin run and the quarterly acceleration, and both were achieved under the departed CEO. On this record the departure is a risk to those conditions rather than their source.

At the last reading the business was accelerating, not fading. Year-on-year revenue growth sped up by 20.6 percentage points, and Data Center supplied +102.5 percentage points of the quarter's growth.

The gross-margin run has a cushion of 3.4 percentage points, 1.69x a typical move, and the company ranks 4 of 63 on gross margin in its industry. The margin assumption is grounded in an unusually strong current position.
The 13.4% a year the price needs sits far below the company's own +100.0% a year over its last three fiscal years. Across the grid of assumptions the requirement stays between 6.5% and 19.7% a year.

Of 40 ten-year spans for filers starting at this size, 0 grew as fast as the price requires, and the implied year-10 revenue is 1.5 times the largest any filer reported. At the industry's 90th-percentile margin of 26.6% the need rises to 28.1% a year.

Working capital is absorbing the earnings. Over the trailing four quarters free cash flow fell $65.87B short of net income as receivables and inventory rose, and inventory days reached 119.3 against 105.6. Excess inventory is what the H20 charge that took margin to 60.5% was for.

The annual trend runs against the quarterly one: fiscal 2026 revenue growth slowed by 48.7 percentage points and Data Center growth by 74.2 percentage points. The above-70% margin test also held in only 6 of 20 past readings.
The first 10-Q covering a post-resignation quarter shows gross margin above 70% and operating margin above 50%.
Quarterly revenue stays above the $96.22B reported for the quarter ended 2026-07-26.
An 8-K names a permanent chief executive, replacing the interim arrangement.
A later 10-Q reports quarterly gross margin below 70%, ending the four-quarter run.
Inventory rises above $31.57B while inventory days stay above 119.3.
The trailing operating margin falls below the 65.2% the reverse DCF assumes.
Accounts receivable fall below the $63.06B of Q2 FY2027.
Trailing cash conversion rises above 0.70x toward 1x.
Deferred revenue holds above the $6.41B of Q2 FY2027.
